original_value: Technological advances, combined with sustained, minimalist consumerism, have raised the popularity of sharing economy platforms like Airbnb and Uber. These platforms are considered to have disrupted traditional industries and revolutionized how consumers interact with their services. The Computer-Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW) community has researched various aspects of the sharing economy; however, it is unclear how novices grow into experts in its various instantiations. In this paper, we present a qualitative investigation of Airbnb hosts, and Facebook groups in which they participate, for an enriched understanding of their learning mechanisms. Drawing on the theory of Legitimate Peripheral Participation (LPP), our findings highlight the learning mechanisms that enable novice hosts to transition from partaking in peripheral roles to becoming integrated members of their (Facebook) communities of practice. We also present recommendations for sharing economy platforms, micro-entrepreneurs, and the online communities that serve them both.

result.paraphrase: Technological advances, together with sustained minimalist consumerism, have boosted the popularity of sharing-economy platforms such as Airbnb and Uber. These platforms are seen as having upended traditional industries and transformed how consumers engage with their services. The Computer-Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW) community has examined multiple facets of the sharing economy; however, it remains unclear how novices develop into experts across its different forms. In this paper, we report a qualitative study of Airbnb hosts and the Facebook groups they belong to, aiming for a deeper understanding of how they learn. Using the theory of Legitimate Peripheral Participation (LPP), our results identify the learning mechanisms that help novice hosts move from peripheral participation to becoming fully integrated members of their Facebook communities of practice. We also offer recommendations for sharing-economy platforms, micro-entrepreneurs, and the online communities that support them both.
